loops.name: AES-128 cipher rounds
loops.parameter: Nr=10 (AES-128, fixed by RTL). No loop-exit logic: the state registers have no enable and run every cycle. dcnt (loaded with 4'hb at ld) only drives done. The 12-cycle protocol fixes the count.
loops.special_iterations: Pre-loop: initial AddRoundKey in the ld_r cycle (cycle 1), sa <= text_in_r ^ w (w = round key 0). Rounds 1..9 (cycles 2..10) are identical: sa <= MixColumns(ShiftRows(SubBytes(sa))) ^ w. Round 10 (last) is special: no MixColumns, separate datapath into text_out (text_out <= ShiftRows(SubBytes(sa)) ^ w). text_out is written every cycle and is correct after cycle 11 (done=1). It is read in cycle 12 = cycle 0 of the next transaction.
loops.fused_with: key expansion: in the cycle where round r uses w = rk_r, the key expander writes rk_{r+1} into w (same cycle)
evidence: aes_cipher_top.v:103-108 (dcnt <= 4'hb on ld, decrement while nonzero)

loops.name: key expansion (round keys 1..10)
loops.special_iterations: Round key 0 = key, loaded when kld=ld (cycle 0); this is not an iteration. Then rk1..rk10 are computed in cycles 1..10, one per cycle. The rcon counter rcnt is reset by kld.
loops.fused_with: AES-128 cipher rounds (same cycle; see above)

notes: Free-running datapath. The loop count is not enforced by the RTL. It comes from dcnt/done and the sampling cycle.

loops.name: key expansion (aes_key_mem CTRL_GENERATE)
loops.parameter: AES_128_NUM_ROUNDS=10, keylen=0. round_ctr_reg runs 0..10. The exit test (round_ctr_reg == num_rounds) is evaluated in the same cycle as the update.
loops.special_iterations: First (r=0): copies key[255:128] (= wrapper key) into key_mem[0] and prev_key1_reg, with no computation. r=1..10: k = f(prev_key1_reg, SubWord(RotWord), rcon). rcon is preset to 8'h8d outside update cycles, so r=0 steps it to 01.
carried_state: keymem.key_mem[0..10] (written here, read by the cipher)
loops.fused_with: none. It is a separate phase (init in cycle 0, GENERATE in cycles 2..12) before the cipher. It time-shares the single 32-bit S-box with the cipher (aes_core sbox_mux, init_state=1).

loops.name: cipher rounds (aes_encipher_block)
loops.parameter: AES128_ROUNDS=4'ha, keylen=0. round_ctr_reg 1..10. Each round = CTRL_SBOX x4 + CTRL_MAIN x1.
loops.special_iterations: Pre-loop: CTRL_INIT (1 cycle), INIT_UPDATE, block_reg <= block ^ key_mem[0]. Rounds 1..9: MAIN_UPDATE (ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey). Round 10 (last): FINAL_UPDATE, no MixColumns, ready <= 1.
loops.fused_with: none (the round key is read combinationally from key_mem[round_ctr_reg])
evidence: aes_encipher_block.v:399-481 (encipher_ctrl FSM; CTRL_INIT 436-443, CTRL_SBOX 445-454, CTRL_MAIN 456-474 with round_ctr_reg < num_rounds at 460)

loops.name: SubBytes word loop (inner, once per cipher round)
loops.parameter: 4 x 32-bit columns, one through the shared 4-byte S-box per cycle (sword_ctr_reg 0..3)
loops.special_iterations: none
carried_state: enc_block.block_w0_reg..block_w3_reg (updated in place, one word per cycle)
loops.fused_with: nested in cipher rounds (40 SubBytes word steps per transaction)

notes: Transaction = init (key expansion, cycles 0..13) + next (encryption, cycles 15..66); the result is read in cycle 68. Wrapper ties encdec=1, keylen=0, key={key,128'h0} (wrap/aes128_enc_top.v:5-6). The decipher block is present but idle (dec_next=0).

loops.name: key expansion (aes_key_mem CTRL_GENERATE)
loops.special_iterations: r=0 copies key[255:128] with no computation; r=1..10 compute

loops.name: cipher rounds (aes_encipher_block)
loops.special_iterations: pre-loop CTRL_INIT whitening with key_mem[0]; rounds 1..9 MAIN_UPDATE; round 10 FINAL_UPDATE without MixColumns

loops.name: SubBytes word loop (inner, once per cipher round)
loops.special_iterations: none

notes: Same RTL and loop structure as aes_sw128, without the wrapper. The AES-256 and decipher paths are synthesized but not executed with the fixed pads. key[127:0] is unused for keylen=0.

loops.name: CORDIC micro-rotations (rotation mode)
loops.special_iterations: none. i=0 uses shift 0 and tanangle(0) in the same datapath. Pre-loop: the init cycle (cycle 0) loads x_i, y_i, theta_i into the rotator registers without rotating. No gain compensation.
carried_state: iteration (5-bit counter; low 4 bits index the shifter and tanangle)
evidence: cordic_iterate.v:366-375 (iteration counter: reset by init, +1 every cycle, no terminal test)
cordic_iterate.v:217-249 (rotator update, direction from sign of z)

notes: There is no terminating counter. The rotator keeps rotating after 16 steps, and iteration[3:0] wraps to 0 at 16. The trip count of 16 comes from the 17-cycle protocol: init in cycle 0, rotations in cycles 1..16, result valid only in cycle 17.

loops.name: folded symmetric tap-pair MAC
loops.parameter: WIDTH=24, 16 odd taps as 8 symmetric pairs. 2 pairs per iteration on 2 multipliers (outer coeff1, inner coeff2). phase counter 1..4.
loops.special_iterations: First iteration: accumulator clear (clear = stb_out_pre[3]), so acc <= product. Post-loop: the centre tap (even sample from srl_even, addr_even=8 for cpi=4) is added in final_sum, then rounded, clipped and output.
carried_state: pipeline registers sum1, sum2, mult1.P, mult2.P, sum_of_prod
loops.fused_with: none. Iterations are pipelined (II=1): SRL read, then pre-add (sum1/sum2), then MULT18X18S, then sum_of_prod, then acc.

notes: Streaming filter. One output per transaction of 2 input strobes (cycles 0 and 4). State carried across transactions: SRL16E data in srl_odd_a..d (four copies of the 16 odd samples), srl_even, odd, and the round_sd error-feedback register (round_in). Because of pipeline latency the loop and the output fall in the next 8-cycle frame.

loops.name: CRC bit steps (C: for (i=0;i<8;i++))
loops.parameter: i<8 (C). Bambu -O1 -fno-unroll-loops builds an FSM self-loop in S_1. The exit test (reg_1 + 1 == 8) runs in the same state as the body.
loops.special_iterations: none. Pre-loop S_0: ans = crc ^ (onech << 8), i = 0. Post-loop S_2: done (done_port registered).
evidence: icrc1.v:494-510 (S_1 loop state, exit to S_2)
icrc1.v:398-412 (i+1, compare with const 8; const_2 at 357-358)

notes: The source is C compiled by Bambu HLS. The loop structure is that of the C source and of the generated FSM. Timing: start in cycle 0, loop in cycles 1..8, done in cycle 9.

loops.name: restoring division bit steps
loops.parameter: quotient_msk = 1<<31 shifted right until 0 (32 bits). DIVU (pcpi_insn 0x02b55533).
loops.special_iterations: none in the loop. Pre-loop start cycle: operand load, no sign change for DIVU, divisor = rs2 << 31. Post-loop finish cycle (quotient_msk == 0): pcpi_rd <= quotient (outsign = 0 for DIVU), pcpi_ready.

notes: Timing: decode in cycles 0..1, start in cycle 2, iterations in cycles 3..34, finish in cycle 35, pcpi_ready in cycle 36.

loops.name: PRESENT-80 rounds
loops.parameter: round counter 1..31 (5-bit, wraps to 0). No exit logic. The 32-cycle protocol fixes the count.
loops.special_iterations: none in the loop. Each round: addRoundKey (kreg[79:16]), 16 S-boxes, pLayer. The final whitening with K32 is not an iteration: odat = dreg ^ kreg[79:16] is combinational and equals the ciphertext in cycle 32 (= load cycle of the next transaction, round==0).
loops.fused_with: key schedule: kreg <= update(kreg, round) in the same cycle as the round (31 key updates)
evidence: present_encrypt.v:50-53, 70 (key update: rotate 61, S-box, XOR round)

notes: Free-running datapath. The bench patch only comments out the PRINT_TEST_VECTORS define (line 26).

loops.name: restoring shift-subtract division
loops.parameter: N=32, Q=15 (defaults). reg_count counts N+Q-1=46 down to 0, giving N+Q iterations.
loops.special_iterations: Last iteration (reg_count==0) is special. It also sets reg_done, copies reg_quotient <= reg_working_quotient and sets overflow. The copy is nonblocking in the same edge that sets quotient bit 0, so bit 0 never reaches the output (o_quotient_out[0] is always 0). The overflow test also uses the old working quotient. Pre-loop start cycle: left-align operands, sign = XOR of signs.
evidence: qdiv.v:86-105 (body: shift 87, compare/subtract 91-94, stop at reg_count==0 97-102, copy 99)

notes: Timing: start in cycle 0, iterations in cycles 1..47, o_complete from cycle 48 (= cycle 0 of the next transaction).

loops.name: restoring shift-subtract division
loops.special_iterations: Last iteration (reg_count==0): output copy before bit 0 lands, so the output LSB is always 0. Overflow uses the old working quotient.

notes: Period 24 = N+Q+1.

loops.name: restoring shift-subtract division
loops.special_iterations: Last iteration (reg_count==0): output copy before bit 0 lands, so the output LSB is always 0. Overflow uses the old working quotient.

notes: Period 96 = N+Q+1.

loops.name: shift-and-add multiplication over multiplicand bits
loops.parameter: N=32, Q=15 (defaults). reg_count counts 0..N. The exit test reg_count==N is in the same cycle as the body, giving N+1 iterations.
loops.special_iterations: Iteration reg_count=N-1 reads reg_multiplicand_temp[N-1], which is always 0 (the register is loaded from i_multiplicand[N-2:0]), so it never adds. The last iteration (reg_count=N) is special. It reads reg_multiplicand_temp[N], out of range of [N-1:0] (x in Verilog semantics), and it sets reg_done and overflow. The overflow test uses the result before this cycle's add. Pre-loop start cycle: load magnitudes, sign = XOR of signs.
evidence: qmults.v:73-88 (body: bit test 74, add 75, shift 77, count 78, stop at reg_count==N 81-87)

notes: The out-of-range read in the last iteration is undefined in the RTL. The reference /home/jiahao/hal/algorithm_recovery/evaluation/program_checks/e5_refs/qmults.py states that the Yosys netlist resolves it to bit 0, giving one extra add of (|b| << N) when |a| is odd. I did not verify this in the netlist. Period 34 = N+2.

loops.name: shift-and-add multiplication over multiplicand bits
loops.special_iterations: reg_count=15 never adds (bit always 0). The last iteration, reg_count=16, reads an out-of-range bit (x in RTL), sets done and overflow (pre-add value).

notes: Same out-of-range caveat as qmults. Period 18.

loops.name: shift-and-add multiplication over multiplicand bits
loops.special_iterations: reg_count=63 never adds (bit always 0). The last iteration, reg_count=64, reads an out-of-range bit (x in RTL), sets done and overflow (pre-add value).

notes: Same out-of-range caveat as qmults. Period 66.

loops.name: SHA-256 compression rounds
loops.parameter: SHA256_ROUNDS=63. t_ctr_reg 0..63 in CTRL_ROUNDS; the exit test (t_ctr_reg == 63) is in the same cycle as the round.
loops.special_iterations: none in the loop. Pre-loop CTRL_IDLE+init (1 cycle): a..h and H0..H7 <= H(0) (mode=1), w_mem <= block, t_ctr <= 0. Post-loop CTRL_DONE (1 cycle): H_i <= H_i + a..h. Rounds t<16 read W from w_mem[t]; rounds t>=16 use the computed w_new.
carried_state: core.H0_reg..H7_reg (constant during the loop, used in the feed-forward)

loops.name: message schedule W_16..W_63
loops.special_iterations: none. In rounds t<16 there is no schedule step (w_mem is not shifted).
loops.fused_with: compression rounds. w_new is computed combinationally and feeds t1 in the same cycle as round t, and w_mem shifts in the same cycle.

notes: Top sha256 is a register interface (sha256.v:162-260). The 16 block-word writes (cycles 0..15) and 8 digest reads (cycles 84..91) follow the address bus driven by the protocol; the RTL has no counter for them. init reaches the core as init_reg in cycle 17, rounds run in cycles 18..81, DONE is cycle 82, and digest_reg is latched at the edge that ends cycle 83. The RTL is secworks/sha256 837c5cc. The e7/sha256_lattice/src copies are byte-identical to bench_candidates/secworks_sha256/src/src/rtl. The netlist is third party (Synplify). Only the protocol's side-by-side check ties it to this RTL. I did not check the netlist's provenance.

loops.name: SHA-256 compression rounds
loops.parameter: round counter 1..64 (7-bit); round r does step t=r-1
loops.special_iterations: Pre-loop round 0 (cycle 1): A..H and H0..H7 <= H(0) (cmd[2]=0, first block), W0/Wt <= text_i, no compression. The last step t=63 (round 64) is special: it is fused with the feed-forward (A <= next_A + H0, ..., H <= G + H7), then round <= 0 and busy <= 0. Steps t=0..15 use input words (Wt latched from text_i); t=16..63 use scheduled words.
evidence: sha256.v:550-626 (rounds 16..63: shift W, Wt <= next_Wt, compress)

loops.name: message schedule W_16..W_63
loops.special_iterations: none
loops.fused_with: compression rounds. W_{t+1} is computed in the cycle of step t and registered in Wt, one cycle ahead of use.

loops.name: message word input (I/O)
loops.special_iterations: word 0 is in round 0 (pre-loop cycle); words 1..15 are in rounds 1..15
evidence: sha256.v:313-314 (round 1; same pattern in each case arm through round 14 at 521-522)

loops.name: digest readout (I/O)
loops.special_iterations: none
evidence: sha256.v:734-771 (read_counter <= 7 on cmd[0]; text_o <= word[read_counter]; decrement)

notes: Timing: command in cycle 0, rounds 0..64 in cycles 1..65, read command in cycle 68, digest words in cycles 71..78.

loops.name: SHA-256 compression rounds
loops.special_iterations: none in the loop. Pre-loop CTRL_IDLE+init (cycle 0): H(0) into a..h and H0..H7, block into w_mem. Post-loop CTRL_DONE (cycle 65): H += a..h. Rounds t<16 read w_mem[t].

loops.name: message schedule W_16..W_63
loops.special_iterations: none
loops.fused_with: compression rounds (w_new used in t1 in the same cycle as round t)

notes: The 512-bit block is a parallel input. Period 66 = 1 + 64 + 1.

loops.name: SHA-256 compression rounds
loops.parameter: SHA256_ROUNDS=63, t_ctr_reg 0..63; mode bit written 1 by the control word
loops.special_iterations: none in the loop. Pre-loop init cycle: H(0), w_mem <= block_reg[0..15]. Post-loop CTRL_DONE: H += a..h.

loops.name: message schedule W_16..W_63
loops.special_iterations: none

notes: Same RTL as sha256_lattice. The four files are byte-identical to bench_candidates/secworks_sha256/src/src/rtl at 837c5cc. Register file block_reg and digest_reg are written and read through the address bus (sha256.v:162-260); there is no RTL loop for the I/O.

loops.name: PRESENT-80 rounds
loops.parameter: round_counter 1..31 (5-bit, wraps). No exit logic. The 33-cycle protocol fixes the count.
loops.special_iterations: none in the loop. Pre-loop: key_load in cycle 0 (key <= data_i), data_load in cycle 1 (state <= data_i[63:0], round_counter <= 1). Rounds run in cycles 2..32. The final K32 whitening is combinational: data_o = state ^ key[79:16], valid in cycle 33 = cycle 0 of the next transaction.
loops.fused_with: key schedule: key <= key_update(key, round_counter) in the same cycle as the round
evidence: present_encryptor_top.v:72-92 (load/round always block; round_counter <= 1 at 83, +1 at 87)

notes: Free-running. The datapath keeps iterating until the next key_load.

loops.name: folded symmetric tap-pair MAC
loops.parameter: USE_DSP48E=0 (chparam). 3 coefficients (coeffphase1_1..3) times pre-added sample pairs (6 taps). count 0..2.
loops.special_iterations: none in the loop. _sum is cleared on ready, after the result is latched into filter_out, so each output starts from 0. Post-loop: ready, filter_out <= sum, ce_out.
loops.fused_with: none. Pipelined with II=1: pre-add (active), multiply (active_d1), accumulate (active_d2).
evidence: fir_decim.v:95-103 (active set on clk_enable && phase==1, cleared at count==2)

notes: Streaming decimate-by-2 filter. Transaction = 2 samples (clk_enable in cycles 0 and 5). The phase-1 sample (cycle 0) triggers the loop. The phase-0 sample (cycle 5) is used by the next transaction. State carried across transactions: storage0[0..11], storage1[0..11] (bit-sliced 4-deep delay lines, positions 0..2 read) and phase.

loops.name: folded 2-step tap-pair MAC on one multiplier
loops.parameter: WIDTH=18. 7-tap halfband [A 0 B 0.5 B 0 A]. Step 1 = B pair (d2+d4), step 2 = A pair (x[n]+d6).
loops.special_iterations: First step is special: accum <= centre tap (middle_d1) + product (go_d2) instead of accumulating. Second step: accum += product (go_d3). The two steps take different operands through the go_d1 mux. No counter. The steps are sequenced by the one-hot strobe chain go -> go_d1 -> go_d2 -> go_d3 -> go_d4.
loops.fused_with: none (pipelined: multiply in go_d1/go_d2, accumulate in go_d2/go_d3)
evidence: small_hb_dec.v:115-121 (accum init at go_d2, add at go_d3)

notes: Synthesis = synth/small_hb_dec (sha256 1f952afd... matches the contract). Streaming. State carried across transactions: delay line d1..d6, data_rnd_d1, phase, and error-feedback registers of both round_sd instances. It may be fairer to call this a fixed 2-step schedule than a loop. See the low-confidence list.

loops.name: shift-add partial products (MULL, Baugh-Wooley form)
loops.parameter: md_op=MULL(0), signed_mode=0, data_ind_timing=1 (no early exit), mult_en held 1. multdiv_count 31..1 in MD_COMP. One step for each bit of the 33-bit sign-extended op_b.
loops.special_iterations: Step 0 (MD_IDLE) is special: it loads the operands and sets accum = pp0 directly, without the ALU add. Steps 1..31 (MD_COMP, 31 cycles) are identical: accum += pp_k, op_a <<= 1, op_b >>= 1. Step 32 (MD_LAST) does the same accum add but sets valid_o, puts out result = res_adder_l[31:0] combinationally, and returns to MD_IDLE. For unsigned operands pp32 is 0 in the low 32 bits. So 31 uniform body iterations plus a peeled first and last step, 33 cycles in total.
loops.fused_with: none (the accumulate uses the shared ALU adder)
evidence: ibex_multdiv_slow.sv:245-257 (MD_COMP: count-1, exit at multdiv_count_q==1 at 255-256)

notes: Period 33 = IDLE + 31 x COMP + LAST. The FSM restarts at once because mult_en is held 1.

loops.name: restoring shift-subtract division
loops.special_iterations: Last iteration (reg_count==0) copies the working quotient before bit 0 lands, so the output LSB is always 0. Overflow uses the old value.

notes: Same synthesized netlist as E5 qdiv (synth/qdiv/qdiv.json, sha256 c37c9e45... = contract).

The body changes by stage: f = Ch for t<20, Parity for 20..39, Maj for 40..59, Parity for 60..79, and Kt is one of 4 constants (registered one cycle ahead).

no loop. The C source (module.c:16-59) is straight-line: 16 multiplications and 12 additions. Bambu with 1 multiplier (constraints_ui_mult1.xml) schedules it as a linear 15-state FSM S_0..S_14 with no back edge except the return to S_0 (gen_shared/arf.v:852, 938-1071). loops.parameter: ROUNDS_A=12, UROL=1. round_cnt_q counts 12 down to 1; the round constant index is 12 - round_cnt.
loops.special_iterations: none. Pre-loop: state <= IV || K || N (ld_npub_done). Post-loop: KADD_2 (x3 ^= K[0..63], x4 ^= K[64..127]).

loops.name: associated-data block loop
loops.parameter: AD = 16 bytes = 1 full 128-bit block, plus the padding block that follows a full final block (schedule CSV ascon_aead128enc_ad16_pt16_v1.csv)
loops.special_iterations: Block 1: ABS_AD absorbs 4 words, then PRO_AD (p^8). Block 2 (last) is special: PAD_AD XORs the pad bit into x0 in 1 cycle, absorbs no data, then PRO_AD (p^8).

loops.name: p^8 rounds after each AD block (inner, PRO_AD)
loops.special_iterations: none
loops.fused_with: nested in the AD block loop (16 rounds in total)

loops.name: plaintext block loop
loops.parameter: PT = 16 bytes = 1 full block, plus the padding block
loops.special_iterations: Block 1: ABS_MSG absorbs 4 PT words and emits 4 CT words, then PRO_MSG (p^8). Block 2 (last) is special: PAD_MSG XORs the pad bit in 1 cycle and is not followed by p^8. Domain separation (DOM_SEP, x4 ^= 1<<63) comes before block 1. After block 2: KADD_3 (x2, x3 ^= K).

loops.special_iterations: none

loops.special_iterations: none. Pre-loop KADD_3. Post-loop KADD_4 (x3, x4 ^= K), then SQZ_TAG.

loops.name: word-serial I/O loops (key, nonce, AD, PT/CT, tag)
loops.parameter: CCW=32, W128=4. word_cnt_q 0..3 for each 128-bit item: key load (LD_KEY), nonce (LD_NPUB), AD absorb (ABS_AD), PT absorb/CT out (ABS_MSG), tag out (SQZ_TAG).
loops.special_iterations: Last word (word_cnt_q == 3) triggers the *_done transition.

notes: Ascon-AEAD128 encryption, AD 16 B, PT 16 B. I traced the FSM by hand over 75 cycles: IDLE 1, LD_KEY 4, LD_NPUB 4, INIT 12, KADD_2 1, ABS_AD 4, PRO_AD 8, PAD_AD 1, PRO_AD 8, DOM_SEP 1, ABS_MSG 4, PRO_MSG 8, PAD_MSG 1, KADD_3 1, FINAL 12, KADD_4 1, SQZ_TAG 4. This agrees with the fsm_state column of the schedule CSV. One shared asconp round function runs 48 rounds per transaction (12 + 8 + 8 + 8 + 12). The block-loop counts hold only for these fixed lengths. The netlist is from conv/ascon_core_v1.v (sv2v, V1).
